blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Job runs a task until it finishes, instead of keeping it running. It comes from the batch/v1 API.
blocks.why: Use a Job for one-off work, such as a database migration or a report.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Job, from the batch/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to check the Job and read its output.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Job
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once

blocks.title: Don't restart when done
blocks.what: The Pod template sets restartPolicy to Never, so a finished container is not started again.
blocks.why: Jobs only allow Never or OnFailure. The usual Pod default, Always, would restart the task forever.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Job, because its Pods would restart after finishing.
blocks.comment: Run each Pod once. The Job decides about retries.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A busybox container prints a message and exits.
blocks.why: When the container exits successfully, the Job is marked Complete.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Job, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: The task: print a message and exit
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: hello
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from a Job"]

blocks.title: How many retries?
blocks.what: backoffLimit is how many times the Job retries a failed Pod before giving up.
blocks.why: Retries help with short failures. A low number stops a broken task from retrying for long.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the default of six retries.
blocks.comment: Give up after two failed retries
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: hello
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from a Job"]

blocks.title: Run it on a schedule
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a CronJob, which creates a Job on a schedule.
blocks.why: Use a CronJob for repeating work, such as nightly backups.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file has only the one-off Job.
blocks.comment: A second object: a CronJob that runs a Job on a schedule
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: hello
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from a Job"]
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-every-minute

blocks.title: When and what
blocks.what: The schedule uses cron format. Five stars mean every minute.
blocks.why: jobTemplate is the Job to create each time. It has the same spec as the Job above.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the CronJob, because it needs a schedule and a jobTemplate.
blocks.comment: Every minute, create a Job from this template
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: hello
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from a Job"]
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-every-minute
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:

blocks.title: The scheduled task
blocks.what: Each run starts a busybox container that prints the time and exits.
blocks.why: OnFailure restarts a failed container in place. This block makes the file ready to apply.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the CronJob, because its Jobs would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: The task each scheduled Job runs
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: hello-once
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: hello
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello from a Job"]
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-every-minute
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: hello
              image: busybox:1.37.0
              command: ["sh", "-c", "date && echo Hello from a CronJob"]

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API group and version. Jobs and CronJobs are in batch/v1.
notes.Job:kind: The type of object to create. A Job runs a task until it finishes.
notes.CronJob:kind: The type of object to create. A CronJob creates Jobs on a schedule.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Job:metadata.name: The Job's name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.CronJob:metadata.name: The CronJob's name. Each Job it creates gets this name plus a number.
notes.spec: The desired state of this object.
notes.spec.backoffLimit: How many failed retries are allowed before the Job gives up. The default is 6.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for the Pods this Job runs.
notes.spec.template.spec.restartPolicy: Never: a finished or failed container is not restarted in the same Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: The task: print a message, then exit so the Job completes.
notes.spec.schedule: When to run, in cron format: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
notes.spec.jobTemplate: The Job to create on each run.
notes.spec.jobTemplate.spec: The Job's spec, the same as in a Job file.
notes.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template: The Pod template for each scheduled Job.
notes.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.rest: OnFailure: restart a failed container in the same Pod.
notes.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.cont: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
The task: print the time and a message, then exit.

tryIt.result: Prints job.batch/hello-once created and cronjob.batch/hello-every-minute created.
hello-once shows Complete. A new hello-every-minute Job appears each minute.
Removes both, including the Jobs the CronJob created.

questions.question: Why is restartPolicy Never on line 9?
answers: A Job’s Pod should stop when the task ends
It stops the Job from running
questions.explain: A Job runs a task to the end. A Pod that always restarted would never finish.

questions.question: How often does hello-every-minute run?
questions.explain: Five stars mean every minute of every hour of every day. Each run creates a new Job.

questions.question: What does backoffLimit: 2 do?
answers: Retries a failed task up to two times
questions.explain: If the task fails, the Job tries again. After two retries, the Job is marked failed.

fix.message: The CronJob "hello-every-minute" is invalid: spec.schedule: Invalid value: "* * * *": expected exactly 5 fields, found 4: [* * * *]
fix.explain: A schedule needs five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week. This one has four.
